CORAM:
HON'BLE

MRS. JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1. Heard the arguments of both sides.
2.
This appeal is filed against the judgment and award of the Tribunal in MVC No.2746/2022 dated 17.10.2023.
The injured claimant met with an accident on 05.04.2022 NC: 2026:KHC:6662 HC-KAR and filed claim petition claiming compensation of  10,00,000/-.
Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted an amount of  5,02,560/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from date of petition till deposit.
Aggrieved by the said order, the appellant preferred this appeal.
3. The claimant mainly contended that he sustained grievous injuries.
The doctor assessed the disability as 40% to the right lower limb and 13% to the whole body.
But the Tribunal erred in taking the same as 10%.
The claimant was working as a delivery boy and earning  20,000/- per month.

sentences.text: But, the Tribunal has taken only national income of  15,500/- per month.
The amounts granted under the other heads is meager.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of the compensation.
4. The claimant met with an accident.
Though claimant stated that he was earning  20,000/- per month, he has not filed any income proof.
He met with an accident in the NC: 2026:KHC:6662 HC-KAR year 2022.
As per the chart prepared by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the Tribunal has rightly taken the national income of  15,500/- per month and he was aged 22 years and the multiplier is 18.

He stated that as per X-ray, the claimant has sustained united patella fracture with broken implants in situ and thus, accessibility of right lower limb as 40% and the disability of the whole body as 13%.
The Tribunal has taken the functional disability as 10% without any basis.
Considering the medical evidence, this Court finds it reasonable to take the disability as 1/3 of 40 i.e. 13%.

The NC: 2026:KHC:6662 HC-KAR loss of future earning capacity comes to 15,500/-x12x18x13% =
4,35,240/-.
Appellant incurred  46,260/- towards medical expenses as per Ex.P11 and it is confirmed and he was hospitalized for fourteen days

Considering his occupation, age, nature of injuries, period of hospitalization and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of  50,000/- for pain and suffering,  25,000/- for loss of amenities and  30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
He might not have attended any other work at least for a period of three months.
Therefore,  15,500/- x 3 months =  46,500/- towards loss of income during laid up period,  15,000/- towards future medical expenses.
The total compensation comes to  6,48,000/- as against  5,02,562/- awarded by the Tribunal.

7. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation:

sentences.text: Conveyance, Food, 30,000 Nourishment and Attendant, charges 7. Loss of income during laid up 46,500 period and rest period Total 6,48,000 8.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.5,02,560/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.6,48,000/-.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,45,440/-
(Rs.6,48,000/- - Rs.5,02,560/-).
9.
The Insurance Company has already deposited the award amount before the Tribunal.

Hence, respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,45,440/- before the Tribunal with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
NC: 2026:KHC:6662 HC-KAR 10.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed-in-part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 16.01.32025 passed in M.V.C.No.376/2022 by the IV Additional Judge and MACT and ACJM, Bengaluru (SCCH-6), is hereby modified holding that the appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,45,440/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.

(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount of Rs.1,45,440/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, before the Tribunal, within a period of one month from the date of this judgment.
NC: 2026:KHC:6662 HC-KAR
( iv )
On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
(v) As per the order in I.A.No.1/2024 dated 05.02.2026, the appellant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 165 days.
(vi) Draw award accordingly.
